claims.text: The premelting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by an interplay between internal structural disorder and thermal energy.
The melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by an interplay between internal structural disorder and thermal energy.
High-temperature in situ TEM can directly observe and elucidate the proposed disorder-dependent premelting and melting behavior.
The proposed experiment compares high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles having different compositions and internal structures.
Temperature and environment are varied during high-temperature in situ TEM characterization.
Internal structural disorder is the structural mediator of premelting and melting.
Heating induces changes in the nanoparticles' internal structure.
Heating induces changes in the nanoparticles' composition.
Premelting or melting will be accompanied by changes in nanoparticle shape.
Premelting or melting will be accompanied by changes in nanoparticle size.
Premelting or melting will be accompanied by changes in nanoparticle composition.
Nanoparticles with low internal structural disorder provide a baseline against which disorder-dependent behavior can be assessed.
Temperature and external environment may affect nanoparticle thermal behavior independently of internal structural disorder.
Sample preparation and instrumentation constrain the range over which high-temperature in situ TEM can test the hypothesis.
If premelting and melting behavior does not correlate with internal structural disorder, the hypothesis is falsified.
